title: Delivery
description: §6.5's Delivery — {envelope, opened: bool, payload?, reason?, returnReceipt?}. It lives here and not in spec/schemas/ because §18.5 fixes the fourteen files there by name and Delivery is not among them: §6.5 defines it in prose, as the shape inbox returns, and adding a fifteenth file would be a specification change (§1.7).

payload.description: Present exactly when opened is true. THE BYTES, base64 — the same alphabet send.input.schema.json accepts them in. A rendering of them as UTF-8 text may appear in the tool's text block, labelled as a rendering; it never replaces them here.

reason.description: §6.5's reasons on an unopened delivery. None of these is a failure of the tool (P-12).

returnReceipt.title: PendingReceipt
returnReceipt.description: §6.5's fourth field: THE PENDING SCHEDULE, read off the lane's `transaction` operation, so that `ack` can sign it (§10.4). This named urn:wishmail:0.5:return-receipt until 2026-09-11 and that was wrong on §6.5's own words — a §5.8 ReturnReceipt does not exist until `ack` has signed and the network has executed, so the $ref named an object no delivery can ever carry. Corrected here rather than accommodated in the handler, because there was nothing to accommodate.

scheduleId.description: The HIP-423 schedule the sender created and the recipient signs (§10.4).

sequenceNumber.description: Where the request sits on the lane, so a reader can go and look at it.

consensusTimestamp.description: When the request landed on the lane.

requestedByHeader.description: True where the envelope's own header asked for a receipt (§7.7, `hdr.rr`).
